page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text from top to bottom, with a short heading line "XCV." and the start of the next paragraph below it. Running head at the top. Signature at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

p.i: ciat, eumque ad illius nuptias invitat. Tum Gabel impositio camelis argento, ad nuptias venit, & Tobiam nactus asidentem mensæ amplectitur, & præ gaudio lachrymans, ei gratulatur huiusmodi verbis: Gratias ago Iova Israelitarum Deo, qui te cum hoc viro lætè conjunxerit. Is tibi pro sua misericordia det exi-sta mares liberos, qui Iovæ legi dent operam: L. nam viri optimi, justi, religiosi, & benefici filius es. Felix dicatur uxor tua, parentesque vestri, ita ut natos vestros, & natorum natos, ad tertiam usque quartamque stirpem videatis, sitque vestra progenies Israelitarum Deo, qui regnat in sempiternum, chara. Hic cum omnes Amen fuc-cinuissent, inierunt epulas, & cum Domini reverentia nuptiarum convivium celebrarunt, G. suaq; uxori fausta precatus est Tobias. Tob.9.

page.notes: The page number is printed as 51ȝ (old-style 3); transcribed as 513 with [?]. The running head is printed in large italic capitals. The woodcut-like initial N of "Nullum" is joined to the word. The line "XCV." is a numbered item, so it is kept as a heading. Possible doubtful readings: "asidentem" (printed with an initial long-s-like letter), "exi-sta" (the word is split across lines as "exi-" / "sta", transcribed as printed), and "suaq;" (abbreviation mark uncertain). The final line "su-" continues on the next page.
